task.goal: Write the life this cycle's record produced. Lead with a named interviewed person or a Packet-named place. The feed or tracker line is the weather, never the lede.
task.approach: Long-view approach (Simon Leary): third-person essayist. Treat supplied sports facts as present structure, not as proof of history or collective memory. A metaphor about continuity, load, or change may interpret the Packet but may not add a person, place, institution, event, season, statistic, cause, organizational intention, or citywide belief. Do not write a game recap, Hal elegy, P Slayer fan heat, or Anthony board memo.

creativeBrief.sceneRule: No witnessed room or scene is supplied. Structure and continuity may appear only as clearly interpretive metaphor grounded in the approved present facts.

plan.focus: The 8-1 record as a load-bearing structure that holds through a role change — Quintero to first, Clark and Hernandez at third — and what continuity means when the hands change but the wall does not.

subjects.name: Wilson Shepard
subjects.profile: Wilson Shepard — Head Coach, Oakland Oaks

subjects.name: Mike Paulson
subjects.profile: Mike Paulson — General Manager, Oakland A's & The Oaks

sources.name: Wilson Shepard
sources.quote: Structure is what holds when the names change. I've seen it in my own locker room — we went 0-9 before anyone counted a game, and the structure didn't wobble because the people in it kept doing their jobs. Same thing with the A's right now. Quintero sliding to first, Clark and Hernandez competing at third — that's not a rebuild, that's a system that trusts the next guy in. The record is just the wall. The hands change, but the wall doesn't move if the foundation's real. That's what I tell my guys when they start reading their own headlines: the ranking is a mirror, not a load-bearing beam. What holds is the work, day in and day out.

sources.name: Mike Paulson
sources.quote: Look, the record is the record. Eight and one is eight and one, and nobody's giving it back because the lineup card changed. But the question of whose record it is — that's the wrong way to look at it. The architecture is the organization. The players are the load-bearing walls. You take one out, you brace it, you move on. Quintero sliding to first, Clark and Hernandez at third — that's us bracing. The wall doesn't fall because the hands change. It holds because the foundation was laid right. That's what I tell myself on the days it doesn't hold.

limits.rule: The Packet is what you know, not the fence around what you may write. The approved facts and the ledger are canon: never contradict them, and never import real-world Oakland (its people, businesses, landmarks, troubles). Everything else — the scene, the street, the weather in the room, unnamed people and what they say, new in-world places and businesses, what the city is talking about — is yours to invent; that colour is the job, and it never rewrites a canon fact. A named ledger citizen speaks only in their approved quote or their own page line. Do not brief the record. Open on a person or place living the condition.
